title: Redwood Discovery - Elysium AI Latency & Throughput
summary: Discovery focusing on p95 latency targets, concurrency, streaming, and token/sec benchmarking for Elysium's chat and summarization workloads. Discussed Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs, SOC2/KMS requirements, and next steps to run benchmarks and share security docs.
next_steps: Redwood to share latency benchmark harness and instructions
Redwood to send pricing for Dedicated and Private options
Redwood to share SOC2 and KMS integration docs
Schedule 2-hour technical deep dive benchmark run with SE and Elysium infra team (week of 5/25)

Owner: Jordan Lee | Item: Send pricing sheet for Hosted/Dedicated/Private options and example commit tiers | Due: 2026-05-18
Owner: Priya Reddy | Item: Provide current request patterns and peak concurrency numbers | Due: 2026-05-17
header:
Date: 2026-05-14
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (CTO, Elysium AI), Miguel Torres (ML Engineer), Priya Reddy (Infra Engineer)
transcript:
00:00 Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood. Quick intro, we have Samir here from our SE team. How's everyone?
00:09 Aisha Khan: Hi, thanks Jordan. We're excited, short on time so we'll try to be efficient.
00:13 Miguel Torres: Hey, thanks. We want to focus on latency p95 and throughput for our chat summarization flow.
00:18 Samir Patel: Great, that's exactly what we wanted to focus on. Can you share your current SLOs and traffic patterns?
00:25 Priya Reddy: Sure. Target p95 is 250ms for short chat completions (~64 tokens) and under 800ms for longer summaries (~512 tokens). Peak concurrency about 600 concurrent reqs, sustained 300 during business hours. We also stream responses to the client.
00:45 Jordan Lee: Awesome, that's helpful. To confirm: 600 concurrent, streaming, 64 token quick responses p95 250ms. Do you have token/sec metrics per GPU today?
00:55 Miguel Torres: We're not exposing GPU metrics externally; we measure at app level. Roughly 20 tokens/sec per request for the longer ones but that varies.
01:05 Samir Patel: Ok. So there are a few levers: model choice, quantization, batching, KV cache/prefix caching, and serving mode. Hosted is simplest, Dedicated gives predictable throughput and reserved GPU pools, Private gives you VPC and on-prem. For your p95 targets with streaming and 600 concurrency, we usually recommend Dedicated or Private with autoscaled pools.
01:28 Aisha Khan: We're leaning away from fully hosted for the critical flows because of the SLOs and compliance. We need SOC2 and KMS for key management. How does Redwood handle encryption and audit logs?
01:38 Jordan Lee: We support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) on Dedicated and Private, and we have SOC2 Type II reports we can share. Audit logs and per-request tracing are available via Console. We'll send docs.
01:50 Priya Reddy: Great. For Dedicated sizing, what's your guidance to hit 250ms p95 on 64-token streaming responses at 600 concurrency?
01:59 Samir Patel: It depends heavily on model and batch timing. For example, for an optimized 7B open model quantized to 4-bit with our runtime optimizations, a runtime GPU (A100-class) may serve ~40-60 tokens/sec per GPU in streaming mode under high batching. But p95 latency is more affected by batching window. If you allow 5-10ms batching, we can keep latencies low. For 600 concurrent streaming short responses, you'd likely want a fleet of dedicated GPUs with concurrent request slots tuned — ballpark might be 12-20 GPUs depending on model and exact token/sec.
02:31 Miguel Torres: That variance is big — can we run a benchmark with our prompt templates and payload sizes?
02:37 Samir Patel: Absolutely. We'll provide a benchmark harness that runs token/sec and p95 calculations across sequence lengths and concurrency. We'll also instrument streaming to measure first-byte latency and tail behavior.
02:50 Aisha Khan: On caching — we do many follow-up turns where prefix caching could save a lot. How does Redwood caching work in streaming?
02:58 Samir Patel: We have KV cache reuse at the request-routing layer. For chats, prefix caching reduces compute for repeated context. Streaming still works; the runtime replays KV cache and only computes the new tokens. That reduces tokens/sec demand significantly for multi-turn chats. It's configurable per-model and per-route.
03:20 Priya Reddy: Any gotchas with autoscaling? We run bursts during product launches. We need predictable cold-start behavior.
03:27 Jordan Lee: For Dedicated we offer burst pools and warm capacity options. Cold starts on new model variants can add latency — we recommend pre-warming or canarying. Private on-prem avoids cloud start variability but adds ops overhead.
03:40 Miguel Torres: Competitors we've tested show decent median but poor p95 under concurrency. Are there any Redwood-specific optimizations for tail latencies?
03:48 Samir Patel: Yes — smart routing across model variants and capacity tiers, preemptive KV cache warming for known hot prompts, and priority queues for latency-sensitive traffic. Also we expose token-level tracing so you can correlate cost and latency.
04:05 Aisha Khan: From compliance side, if we choose Private, do you support air-gapped deployments?
04:11 Jordan Lee: Yes, Private can be deployed on-prem and we support air-gapped installs with a private control plane. That includes SSO integrations you asked about and audit logs stored in your environment.
04:22 Priya Reddy: For benchmarks, what metrics should we capture? We want p50/p90/p95/p99, first-byte and last-byte latency, tokens/sec, GPU util, and percent dropped due to overload.
04:33 Samir Patel: That's our typical list. We'll give you a harness that captures those, plus per-route KV cache hit rates and batch sizes.
04:40 Miguel Torres: Streaming specifics: we need first-byte under 120ms for short responses and sustained token throughput per connection above 15 tokens/sec.
04:48 Samir Patel: Understood. We'll measure first-byte and steady-state throughput separately. For hosted, hitting 120ms p95 may be tight at 600 concurrency; Dedicated with reserved slots and tuned batch windows is more likely.
05:02 Aisha Khan: How long to stand up a Dedicated test? We want to run an experiment next week.
05:08 Jordan Lee: We can provision a dedicated test pool in 48-72 hours for a pilot. For Private it takes longer due to infra. We'll need your network info and an infra contact to expedite.
05:16 Priya Reddy: I'll share our VPC CIDR and infra Slack contact after the call.
05:20 Miguel Torres: For model versions: we plan to use an in-house fine-tuned 7B and also try a larger 13B open model for fallback. Any issues serving multiple model variants with routing?
05:31 Samir Patel: No, the platform supports model variant routing by policy. You can route by latency, cost, region, or user cohort, and automatic fallback is supported. For a 7B primary with 13B fallback, we recommend a cheap low-latency variant for primary and the 13B for heavy tails if needed.
05:47 Jordan Lee: Quick note: sometimes Fireflies transcripts mishear product names — apologies if you see Redwood Dedi or Redwoods in the transcript export.
05:54 Aisha Khan: Ha, yep noted.
05:57 Samir Patel: Any constraints on telemetry? Some enterprises restrict tracing. We can do sample rates and filtered logs to meet privacy constraints.
06:06 Priya Reddy: Ok. For SLOs, if we commit to 250ms p95 on short flows, what SLAs do you offer for Dedicated?
06:14 Jordan Lee: Dedicated includes latency and uptime targets in enterprise contracts; specific numeric SLA depends on commit tier. We'll include sample SLA language in the docs we send.
06:22 Miguel Torres: Can you include examples of cost per token for streaming vs non-streaming at different commit tiers?
06:28 Jordan Lee: Yes, we'll include unit economics examples and show how batching and caching reduce per-token costs.
06:34 Aisha Khan: For the benchmark run, who should be present? I want our infra and ML lead in the room.
06:40 Jordan Lee: We'll have Samir and an infra ops engineer on our side and Jordan (AE) for coordination. That should be enough for a 2-hour run.
06:48 Priya Reddy: Sounds good. We'll validate network egress and provide test data sanitized.
06:53 Miguel Torres: One more question: does Redwood expose per-request tokens billed so we can reconcile costs?
06:58 Samir Patel: Yes, we expose token accounting and per-request breakdown in the Console and via APIs.
07:05 Jordan Lee: Ok wrapping up — Samir will send the benchmark harness and runbook, Jordan will send pricing and SOC2/KMS docs, Priya will send VPC details, and we schedule the deep-dive. Anything else?
07:18 Aisha Khan: That's it from us. Thanks.
07:21 Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts and a calendar invite for the benchmark.
07:25 End of recording (approx 45 minutes)
